title: ‘Hanuman Ansh,’ ‘Pyre’ and Shah Rukh Khan Classics Lead International Film Festival of India’s Inflatable Cinema Lineup as NFDC, ESG Renew PictureTime Partnership
description: Vishal Chaturvedi’s hit “Hanuman Ansh” and Vinod Kapri’s “Pyre” will headline a pop-up inflatable cinema at the International Film Festival of Indi
body:
Vishal Chaturvedi’s hit “Hanuman Ansh” and Vinod Kapri’s “Pyre” will headline a pop-up inflatable cinema at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, where the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) have teamed with PictureTime Digiplex again.

	The mobile auditorium is going up on the Kala Academy campus and will serve as a festival hub, screening films every day from Nov. 21 to Nov. 28. PictureTime is known for deploying portable inflatable theaters in underserved areas across India.
	

	The program is split into three strands: Contemporary, Children’s Films and Nostalgia. Alongside “Hanuman Ansh” and “Pyre,” the contemporary selection includes Deepti Pillay Sivan’s Malayalam-language “Achappa’s Album” and Sachin Mohite’s Marathi-language “Kapuskoonda.”

	“Our association with NFDC and IFFI has grown into a meaningful, long-standing partnership, and it is always special for us to return to a festival that brings together the best of Indian and international cinema,” said Sushil Chaudhary, founder and CEO of PictureTime Digiplex.

	Shah Rukh Khan romances dominate the Nostalgia section. Yash Chopra’s “Darr: A Violent Love Story,” “Dil To Pagal Hai,” “Jab Tak Hai Jaan” and “Veer Zaara” will play along with Aditya Chopra’s “Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge.” Kunal Kohli’s “Fanaa” and two Nasir Hussain films, “Yaadon Ki Baarat” and “Hum Kisise Kum Naheen,” round out the strand.

	On the children’s side, Kaushal Oza’s 2026 film “Little Thomas,” with Gulshan Devaiah and Rasika Dugal in the cast and Ranjan Singh among its co-producers, will anchor the morning screenings for schoolchildren. Other family titles include Sai Paranjpye’s “Bhago Bhoot” (2000), Rajeev Sharma’s “Bandu Boxer” (2006), Rajan Khosa’s “Gattu” (2011), Batul Mukhtiar’s “Kaphal-Wild Berries” (2013) and Pankuj Parashar’s “Banarasi Jasoos” (2015).
	

	Chaudhary added: “What makes this edition especially exciting is the range of audiences and cinematic experiences we are looking to bring together. … Equally important for us is extending the festival experience beyond its core venues and delegates, and bringing these films to local communities across Goa so that they too can participate in and feel a part of IFFI.”

	The Goa run caps a busy year for the company. PictureTime also supported the exhibition infrastructure at the Dharamshala International Film Festival and took “Pyre” to audiences in the Indian hinterland.

schema.headline: ‘Hanuman Ansh,’ ‘Pyre’ and Shah Rukh Khan Classics Lead International Film Festival of India’s Inflatable Cinema Lineup as NFDC, ESG Renew PictureTime Partnership

title: ‘Project 11,’ Shot by 11 Directors in 11 Global Cities, Returns on Oh Short Flips (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Project 11,” a 2011 survival thriller made by 11 directors working remotely from 11 cities, will be re-released Nov. 26 as the first title under O
body:
“Project 11,” a 2011 survival thriller made by 11 directors working remotely from 11 cities, will be re-released Nov. 26 as the first title under Oh Short Flips‘ new Classic Shorts vertical.

	The short pits 11 gamers in 11 cities against one another. Each has 11 minutes to live, and only the final survivor wins. Made years before online phenomena such as the Blue Whale Challenge caused alarm worldwide, the film dealt with fears around deadly real-world gaming dares.
	

	Mumbai-based filmmaker Vikas Chandra drove the project, spending months finding 11 directors willing to take part. Their combined crews numbered around 100 people, spread across New York, Los Angeles, Toronto, London, Luxembourg, Tel Aviv, Dar es Salaam, Balochistan, Mumbai, Beijing and Tokyo.

	The directors could not meet in person. All pre-production and storyboarding happened online. To make actors on different continents look as though they shared a frame, the filmmakers matched eyelines, faked over-the-shoulder setups and found lookalike locations in cities such as London and New York, then tied the footage together through lighting, lens choices and choreography.

	The film went from script to finished cut in 149 days. A first version running 25 minutes was trimmed to 11 minutes and 11 seconds.

	Alongside Chandra (Mumbai), the directors are Alessio Giorgetti (New York), Ali Ahmed Brohi (Balochistan), Dharamveer Singh Chauhan (Luxembourg), Ikematsu Hiro (Tokyo), Joseph Cohen (Tel Aviv), Nkumi Mtingwa (Dar es Salaam), Rafal Rakoczy (London), Ryan Singh (Toronto), Sydney Walsh (Los Angeles) and Yi Luo (Beijing).
	

	“Long before the AI times, we made ‘Project 11’ with pure HumInt (Human Intelligence) – one part madness, one part ingenuity and a lot of passion, just like the write-ups called it back then,” Chandra said. “Eleven filmmakers from eleven cities who had mostly never met, connecting over late-night Skype calls, putting serious faith in strangers, and somehow scrambling crew, locations and equipment on a shoestring to pull off one crazy lab experiment in filmmaking.”

	Classic Shorts will bring back well-regarded short films from earlier years that are now hard to come by, aimed at today’s online audiences.

	Producer Ranjan Singh, founder of Oh Short Flips, said six months of releasing shorts on the company’s channel had shown that well-made stories always find an audience. “And we know there are so many classic shorts that are good but not available anywhere for the audience. When we did some inquiries, we realized so many filmmakers would like to release their earlier shorts for the audience to watch. Thus, we’ve decided to release these Classic Shorts also on Oh Short Flips.”

	Singh added that the team made the film on a basic understanding of collaboration. “Even back then when social media wasn’t that popular we found these directors who wanted to tell a story together. Vikas led from the front and ensured the entire process was smooth and coherent. I am extremely proud that we’re starting our Classic Shorts section with ‘Project 11.'”

	Chandra said that, looking back, the film was probably a little ahead of its moment. “It feels good that the film is getting another life now, on a channel dedicated to shorts.”

	The news was unveiled on the sidelines of the WAVES Film Bazaar, the market arm of the International Film Festival of India in Goa.

schema.headline: ‘Project 11,’ Shot by 11 Directors in 11 Global Cities, Returns on Oh Short Flips (EXCLUSIVE)

title: How ‘Hunger Games’ Stars Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson Return for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the ending of “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” now playing in theaters.

	The mutt is out
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the ending of “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” now playing in theaters.

	The mutt is out of the bag: Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson are back for a cameo scene at the end of “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” a prequel to their mega-hit movie franchise from the 2010s. 

	Their returns had been leaked ahead of the movie’s release, but fans who read Suzanne Collins’ novel when it dropped in 2025 shouldn’t be surprised by their inclusion. Despite being a prequel story centering on a young Haymitch Abernathy (played by Joseph Zada), the ending of the “Sunrise on the Reaping” novel jumps ahead for an epilogue featuring adult Haymitch (Woody Harrelson), Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson). The movie follows the plot closely, and gives fans a look at the original trio since their last outing in 2015’s “Mockingjay – Part 2.”
	

	There are several other hints to the original “Hunger Games” series in “Sunrise on the Reaping,” like the inclusion of Katniss’ parents, Burdock Everdeen and Asterid March. Burdock is one of Haymitch’s best friends growing up, and Asterid is his girlfriend. They try to support Haymitch after he wins the Second Quarter Quell, but he pushes them away after suffering so much loss and turns to drinking alone in the Victors’ Village. Near the ending of the movie, Burdock and Asterid hold a baby Katniss in their arms, who locks eyes with Haymitch as he hides and watches them. Asterid was also a friend to Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), who was the original owner of the famous mockingjay pin which eventually ends up in Katniss’ hands.
	

	The “Sunrise on the Reaping” ending jumps ahead to show adult Peeta and Katniss post-“Mockingjay,” living peacefully in Victors’ Village together with Haymitch as their neighbor. They greet Haymitch and wish him a happy birthday before he goes to the meadow to pay tribute to this late love, Lenore Dove (Whitney Peak). He says hi to the geese, something he and Lenore would do as kids. It’s a touching ending that comes full circle with the original stars and Haymitch’s tragic past.

schema.headline: How ‘Hunger Games’ Stars Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson Return for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’

title: Bentonville Film Festival Sets 2027 Dates, Variety’s Producers to Watch Returns for 3rd Year
description: The Bentonville Film Festival will return for its 13th year June 14-20, renewing its partnership with Variety’s 10 Producers to Watch for its third
body:
The Bentonville Film Festival will return for its 13th year June 14-20, renewing its partnership with Variety’s 10 Producers to Watch for its third consecutive year.

	Founded in 2015 by Geena Davis, the festival fosters and celebrates authentic storytelling through film screenings, industry conversations and community experiences.

	“Over the past 12 years, BFF has championed the artistry of thousands of talented filmmakers, creating opportunities to showcase stories that have been overlooked,” Davis said. “As we look ahead to 2027, we remain committed to expanding our reach, connecting filmmakers with audiences and celebrating the power of storytelling to bring people together.”
	

	Leigh Hopkins has also been appointed to BFFoundation’s board of directors after previously serving as the executive vice president and regional CEO for Asia and Mexico for Walmart International.

	“We are thrilled to welcome Leigh to the BFFoundation board,” said Wendy Guerrero, the president and CEO of BFFoundation and the BFF. “His leadership experience, commitment to community and understanding of the region will be valuable as we continue to grow the festival, strengthen our partnerships and expand opportunities for filmmakers and audiences.”

	Hopkins added, “I’m delighted to join the BFFoundation board and be part of a festival that not only brings outstanding films to Bentonville, but also creates meaningful community connections through its year-round programming and events. It’s an honor to help shape what’s ahead for BFF.”

	The 2026 festival featured 34 feature competition films, with winners including Walter Thompson-Hernández’s “If I Go Will They Miss Me” for best narrative and Judd Ehrlich’s “Jane Elliott Against the World” for best documentary.
	

	See key dates for 2027 festival submissions below.

Nov. 20: Early Deadline

title: Bill Hader’s Feature Directorial Debut ‘They Know’ Acquired by Black Bear
description: Black Bear has acquired the North American rights to Bill Hader‘s feature directorial debut “They Know.” Hader also wrote and stars in the horror-t
body:
Black Bear has acquired the North American rights to Bill Hader‘s feature directorial debut “They Know.” Hader also wrote and stars in the horror-thriller with Linda Cardellini. 

	Based on an idea from Hader and his “Barry” collaborator Duffy Boudreau, “‘They Know’ follows a divorced dad who becomes increasingly suspicious and paranoid that his ex-wife’s new mysterious partner is exerting a strange, unsettling influence on their children,” according to an official logline. Further plot details and casting remain under wraps. 
	

	Hader serves as producer with Bob Graf under his Hanarply banner. Alyssa Donovan is co-producer. MRC fully financed the film, which is currently in post-production. FilmNation Entertainment is acting as the worldwide sales agent. “They Know” marks the second collaboration between Black Bear and MRC following the studio’s acquisition of “Honeymoon/Funeral,” which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival. 

	“Bill Hader is a singular talent both in front of and behind the camera, and he has delivered a film in ‘They Know’ unlike anything we’ve ever seen,” said Michael Heimler, president of production & operations at Black Bear. “’They Know’ is authentic, original and bold filmmaking at the highest level, and we couldn’t be more excited to partner with Bill and re-team with our great friends at MRC, who consistently deliver boundary-pushing films that help define their genre.”

	Hader, outside of his eight-season run on “SNL,” is best known for his HBO series “Barry.” The squirmy dramedy about a contract killer with dreams of becoming an actor won 10 Emmys over its four-season run. Hader served as the star and directed several episodes. His most recent big screen bout was voicing the Cat in the Hat in the Warner Bros. adaptation of the classic Dr. Seuss storybook.
	

	Cardellini recently took home her first Emmy for her performance in HBO’s “DTF St. Louis.” She’s also newly leading the cast of Peacock’s “Friday the 13th” prequel series “Crystal Lake” as the soon-to-be-slasher Pamela Voorhees. Her last film role was in Netflix’s family comedy “Nonnas.”

	Black Bear recently released the fantasy romance “Wicker,” starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård. The studio’s upcoming films include Guy Ritchie’s “Wife & Dog,” starring Benedict Cumberbatch, Rosamund Pike and Anthony Hopkins; David Leitch’s “Jason Statham Stole My Bike,” starring Jason Statham and Hannah Waddingham; Nahnatchka Khan’s “Honeymoon / Funeral,” starring Rebecca Ferguson and Greta Lee; “A Woman in the Sun,” starring Renée Zellweger and Sissy Spacek; “Jonah,” starring Lee and Cooper Hoffman; and “Atmosphere,” written and directed by Anna Boden & Ryan Fleck, based on the bestselling book by Taylor Jenkins Reid.

	MRC recently released “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” with John Turturro, “The Love Hypothesis” and “Wuthering Heights.” Upcoming MRC titles include “The Gallerist,” “A Place in Hell” and “Eloise.”

	Deadline was the first to report Black Bear’s acquisition of “They Know.”

schema.headline: Bill Hader’s Feature Directorial Debut ‘They Know’ Acquired by Black Bear

title: Paramount+ Is Down to $2.99 a Month With This Black Friday Deal
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	A lot has
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	A lot has changed at Paramount since last Black Friday, but its streaming discounts are staying the same. The company is bringing back its popular Paramount+ Black Friday deal, offering both its Essential and Premium plans for $2.99 per month for the first two months.

	The limited-time promotion, which launches ahead of Black Friday on Nov. 27, brings both Paramount+ Essential and Paramount+ Premium down to $2.99 per month for the first two months —  a nearly 80% discount on the Premium plan (typically costs $13.99 per month) and a roughly 67% discount on the ad-supported Essential plan (regularly priced at $8.99 per month).
	

	The deal is available through Nov. 30,  just in time for the fourth and final season of “Yellowjackets” set to premiere Nov. 20. The platform is also home to Taylor Sheridan’s expanding television universe, including “Landman,” “Tulsa King,” “1883” and “1923,” alongside original series such as “MobLand,” “Mayor of Kingstown” and “Star Trek: Strange New Worlds.”

	For the same promotional price, subscribers can opt for Paramount+ Premium, which includes commercial-free on-demand viewing, access to Showtime programming, downloads for offline viewing and live streaming of local CBS stations. The Essential tier offers much of the same programming with advertisements, although certain Showtime titles and Premium features are excluded.

	Sports fans can also take advantage of the promotion to stream NFL games airing on CBS, UEFA Champions League matches and UFC programming. Premium subscribers additionally receive access to their local CBS station’s live feed.
	

	To claim the deal, subscribers can sign up directly through Paramount+’s website before Nov. 30. The promotion applies to monthly subscriptions only and is available to new customers and eligible former subscribers, with certain platform restrictions for returning users.

schema.headline: Paramount+ Is Down to $2.99 a Month With This Black Friday Deal

title: ‘War’ Stars Sienna Miller and Dominic West Tussle Over Who Won the Divorce Drama: ‘Gwyneth Paltrow Ran So That the Rest of Us Could Walk’
description:
Nov 19, 2026 7:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘War’ Stars Sienna Miller and Dominic West Tussle Over Who Won the Divorce Drama: ‘Gwyneth Paltrow Ra
body:
Nov 19, 2026 7:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘War’ Stars Sienna Miller and Dominic West Tussle Over Who Won the Divorce Drama: ‘Gwyneth Paltrow Ran So That the Rest of Us Could Walk’
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Courtesy of Simon Emmett, Sky/NOW
	

		
	
				

	SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “War,” which had its season finale on Nov. 19 on HBO and HBO Max in the U.S., and drops on Nov. 20 on Sky and NOW in the U.K.


	The climactic season finale of “War”—  the Sky and HBO drama series starring Sienna Miller and Dominic West as warring spouses — sees an unexpected denouement just as the couple’s increasingly bitter divorce is about to be finalized. With their lawyers still battling it out, the couple bury the hatchet and hammer out their own, more equitable deal. And with that, they walk off into the sunset.

	Written and created by by George Kay (“Hijack”), the series is set to return for a second season with a new case  — and new clients — to occupy the show’s fictional law firms, Taylor & Byrne and Cathcarts. In Season 2, Marisa Tomei, Kelly Macdonald and David Harewood join the cast as the litigants in a high-stakes defamation case.



	

									Courtesy of Ana Blumenkron/Sky/HBO
	



	While Miller and West won’t reprise their roles as actress Carla Duvall and tech billionaire Morgan Henderson, neither seems quite ready to leave their characters behind. In a chat with Variety, both actors repeatedly slipped back into their roles, cheerily arguing over Morgan’s “flirting” with Carla’s barrister (Celia Imrie), Carla’s dalliance with Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) and who really won their explosive — extremely expensive — divorce battle.


	Read on for the full conversation.


	
		Let’s talk about that ending, with your two characters on the beach, seemingly as friends. What were your thoughts when you first read it?	

	Sienna Miller: It was the last thing we ever shot, so that was lovely. And I can’t really remember: A part of me probably wanted something really dramatic and cataclysmic to happen. But at the same time, I defer to the brilliance of George Kay knowing what an audience wants, because he’s written the show that people are devouring. I think the sensationalist in me wanted handbags at dawn [British idiom meaning “a dramatic showdown”], but I also in retrospect think it’s quite lovely that they had that moment. Dom?

	Dominic West: “Handbags at dawn” — that would have been great. I’d have loved handbags at dawn.


	
		Did you feel it was an unexpected ending? Or had George told you in advance?	

	Miller: I think George told us that essentially, this is what’s going to happen: The lawyers screw everything up, and [Carla and Morgan] got there in a much more simple way. So we had an idea — not at the beginning of shooting, but as we were going on — we’re like, “How does it end? What happens?!” You know, nagging like a bunch of kids. We had an inkling that that was what it was, but, again, I was 35 weeks pregnant, so the whole thing is a blur. That’s why I’m hoping Dom can jump in.

	West: I remember my first thoughts were “Fucking hell, what a waste of £10 million” or whatever they spent on the lawyers when they just make it up between themselves. But actually, I think that was the point George was trying to make, and I quite like the idea that they had to go through this terrible process of lawyers and courtroom drama and going to war with each other basically in order to realize actually what they meant to each other. And how they could amicably come to an arrangement where both felt that they’d got what they deserved, and that their relationship had been quantified in a good way, in a just way. 

	But I think that’s the thing that really hit me was “What a fucking waste of £10 million.” But then, if you’re a billionaire, I suppose you do waste £10 million quite happily just to work out how much you like your ex-wife or ex-husband.

	Miller: I do think there’s something very zeitgeist-y — and I’m not sure how he’s done this, George — but the timing of this show is so interesting. I read an article, and it was talking about “Just normalize divorce.” That the process of divorce has become so acrimonious, hellish. The children suffer. It should be something that can be amicable. Obviously, Gwyneth Paltrow ran so that the rest of us could walk. But there is a conscious uncoupling that can be lovely and better for everyone, and it left it left me feeling that it probably should be the goal to avoid conflict and remember why you love this person and how to end it in the nicest way.



	

									Courtesy of Justin Downing/Sky/HBO
	




	
		Did you did you film any alternate endings?	

	Miller: No.

	West: No, we didn’t. But [Kay] didn’t tell us straight away, did he? I don’t think I knew that it was going to end so amicably.

	Miller: I still think I won in court.

	West: I don’t think you did, dear.

	Miller: Well, I think the audience might feel that I did because you couldn’t remember the fucking poem, could you?

	West: Well, I suppose you won in that you got money for ideas and running a business that you had nothing to do with. So in that way, I suppose you were a winner.

	Miller: I hope that, because [Kay] has left it amicable at the end that Dom and I can pop back.



	

									Courtesy of Justin Downing/Sky/HBO
	




	
		Given Carla and Johnny sleep together, it does feel like there’s a way for her to return.	

	West: What, a spinoff with Sienna and Johnny? No way!

	Miller: Have you watched it, Dom?

	West: I haven’t watched it all yet. I’ve only just got Sky, but I’m getting to it. I can’t wait. I watched the first episode six times, and I haven’t managed to see the rest. But I’m on it.

	Miller: One of the cast texted me something very funny, which was “I hope you can come back, but Carla’s such a crazy bitch, you never know she might do something else to get in there.”


	
		That’s true. She might have more legal trouble.	

	Miller: She might.

	West: She’s bound to have more legal trouble.

	Miller: Well, judging by your nefarious behavior in Episode 1, I think it’s coming for you too. Now it’s a hit, we really want to be invited back.

	West: Yeah!


	
		It would be great to see more of Carla and Morgan in the show. And I’m really enjoying this live reenactment, by the way.	

	Miller: Sorry, we haven’t spoken in a while!

	West: It may have ended amicably on set, but it hasn’t really ended amicably between Sienna and I in terms of the characters.



	

									Courtesy of Justin Downing/Sky/HBO
	




	
		I can tell. In terms of filming the series, how did it feel to be cross examined during the court scenes?	

	West: It was really noticeable in court: When I was talking Sienna was sitting right there, and so we’re very close to each other, we can look at each other in the eye. And it was quite thrilling to be putting the boot in, or trying to make war with someone, when you’re sitting right there. I was getting into the moment, and that was quite thrilling, to be so confrontational and to be having a go at Carla, with her being right there. The second thing was being cross-examined by Celia Imrie was quite flirty. In fact, very flirty. She was really flirty, Celia.

	Miller: You say that about everyone, Dom. I think it might be you.

	West: No, no, that was — it was —

	Miller: One thing I particularly love about when Dom answers a question about “War” is he always says “to be at war with each other.” You always drop the name, which I appreciate. I just had to say.

	West: Yeah, no, good. But anyway, let me finish. So yeah, [Imrie] was quite flirty, but that was her strategy and it was in the writing. But Celia really has got such a twinkle that I loved being cross-examined by her.



	

									Courtesy of Justin Downing/Sky/HBO
	




	
		And what about for you, Sienna?	

	Miller: Well, I have been cross-examined [in real life] a few times, I think. I’m pretty sure I have been. Archie Panjabi [who plays Morgan’s barrister] was amazing and quite stern, and I had horrible flu that day, so again, an unhelpful, blurry response. I feel like Carla felt so in-the-right in herself that I wasn’t particularly rattled. It was an intimidating environment and it was a long day, but I quite enjoyed it because I felt like I had the upper hand. Dom would disagree.


	
		You both have been the subject of tabloid stories in real life with regard to your personal lives. Was there any concern about taking on these roles in light of that?	

	Miller: I mean, I definitely have experienced opening the door and being faced with what Carla is faced with. Not anymore, thank God. But I only read the first script when I signed on. So you’re taking a gamble. I mean, I knew she was an actress and I knew she was famous, so I assumed there might be some of that, but I didn’t really — I don’t think I want to play an actress again. Unless it’s Carla coming back in “War.”

	
		Did you collaborate with George on any of those scenes of Carla dealing in the public eye?	

	Miller: Not particularly, no, because I didn’t know where it would all go or the spins that it would take. And no, it’s not particularly interesting for me to relive those moments or those years, but I do have an innate knowledge of them, and I suppose that’s interesting for people to see. I feel like I’m so different to Carla herself that maybe her response was an interesting thing to explore.
	

	
		And what about for you, Dominic?	

	West: Yeah, I mean, I suppose I did have hesitations about it, but in practice, in doing it, what was quite thrilling was the thought of a billionaire getting the sort of scrutiny that the British press normally reserves for young actresses. I found that quite a thrill.



	This interview has been edited and condensed.



	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: ‘War’ Stars Sienna Miller and Dominic West Tussle Over Who Won the Divorce Drama: ‘Gwyneth Paltrow Ran So That the Rest of Us Could Walk’

title: Lakers’ Official History Book Gets $9,600 Limited Edition With Magic Johnson Handprints, Staples Center Hardwood and Rare Artwork
description:

	The Los A
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	The Los Angeles Lakers’ $100 coffee-table book is getting a five-figure upgrade.

	Luxury art-book publisher Taschen and the Lakers have unveiled two limited-edition versions of “Lakers: An Official History of the Purple & Gold,” featuring original handprints from Showtime-era legends, authenticated hardwood from the former Staples Center court and exclusive artwork signed by Magic Johnson and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.


	The new releases, announced Thursday, are limited to 1,100 copies worldwide, with 1,000 Collector’s Editions priced at $2,400 each and just 100 Art Editions retailing for $9,600.
	

		

			
			
			
			
	

	
					
		

										LIMITED RELEASE						

					Lakers: An Official History of the Purple & Gold		

		
	

	Both versions include the original 528-page book, housed in a custom leather clamshell box designed by Jeff Hamilton, the fashion designer known for his elaborate leather jackets commemorating the Lakers’ championship victories in 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2020.

	Each box also contains an authenticated piece of hardwood from the original Staples Center floor, where the Lakers won five championships and Kobe Bryant played his final NBA game. Collectors will receive an original handprint from one of seven Showtime-era figures — Johnson, Abdul-Jabbar, James Worthy, Michael Cooper, Kurt Rambis, Byron Scott or Pat Riley — with the identity revealed upon delivery.

	The $9,600 Art Edition takes things a step further, adding a large-format print of Ernie Barnes’ “Fastbreak,” originally commissioned by the Lakers in 1987. The 41-by-24.5-inch artwork depicts the team in the midst of its Showtime era and features seven signature plates hand-signed by the players and coach portrayed in the painting. Each print is numbered and authenticated by the Estate of Ernie Barnes.
	

	The limited editions arrive nearly two months after Taschen released the standard version of the book in September. Abdul-Jabbar wrote the foreword, Lakers governor Jeanie Buss contributed the introduction and former coach Phil Jackson penned the afterword. Other contributors include Johnson, O’Neal, Pau Gasol, LeBron James, Luka Dončić, Jack Nicholson, Paula Abdul, Flea and Lou Adler.

	“The Lakers have had an extraordinary impact on basketball and pop culture, and we wanted this book to capture the full scope of that influence, from the game itself to art, fashion, music, and beyond,” Tobak said in a statement. “The Limited Edition takes that vision a step further, bringing together rare memorabilia, artwork, and personal contributions from the people who helped shape the team’s history.”

	Both limited editions are available now through Taschen’s website.

schema.headline: Lakers’ Official History Book Gets $9,600 Limited Edition With Magic Johnson Handprints, Staples Center Hardwood and Rare Artwork

title: Two Directors, One Oscar: Can Lord and Miller, Los Javis, Fielder and Oppenheim or the Esiri Brothers Break Through?
description:
Are two directors better than one?

	Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Phil Lord and Chris Miller and Nigeria’s
body:
Are two directors better than one?

	Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Phil Lord and Chris Miller and Nigeria’s Esiri brothers are chasing a prize the Academy’s Director Branch has handed to a duo only three times in its history.

	Looking at the two-name directing teams in this year’s Oscar race, artistic collaboration seems to be having a moment. Not everyone sees it that way.


	“If you need two of you to make the film, then I think that’s a problem,” one prominent member of the Directors Branch bluntly tells Variety.
	

	Fielder and Oppenheim turned Elizabeth Holmes’ saga into the slippery A24 documentary “You Can See Everything.” Calvo and Ambrossi, the Spanish duo known as Los Javis, are carrying their country’s international feature hopes with “La Bola Negra.” Lord and Miller reunited behind the camera for Amazon MGM’s sci-fi swing “Project Hail Mary.” And twin brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri helmed Neon’s ambitious “Clarissa,” a reimagining of “Mrs. Dalloway.”

	All four teams face a stubborn piece of Academy history: The Directors Branch does not like splitting statuettes. In 98 years, only four directing duos have received best director nominations (one of them twice). This year, several are within earshot of nods.

	Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins got there first for 1961’s “West Side Story.” Their partnership was so combustible that Robbins was fired mid-production for running over schedule and budget. He retained his credit and collected the Oscar.

	Warren Beatty and Buck Henry followed with “Heaven Can Wait” (1978), but lost to Michael Cimino (“The Deer Hunter”). Joel and Ethan Coen scored for the best picture winner “No Country for Old Men” (2007), and were nominated again for the Western remake “True Grit” (2010), losing out to Tom Hooper (“The King’s Speech”). The most recent winners, Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, aka the Daniels, took home the prize for “Everything Everywhere All at Once” (2022).
	



	

					Chris Miller, Phil Lord and Ryan Gosling on the set of “Project Hail Mary”
									Amazon MGM Studios
	



	History suggests that longtime professional partnerships are the key to acceptance. Wise and Robbins were a filmmaker and a choreographer brought together by a studio. The Daniels met making music videos. The Coens remain the only sibling duo recognized.

	The Academy has repeatedly overlooked pairings, even in the face of precursor support. Jonathan Dayton and Valerie Faris, the married filmmakers behind “Little Miss Sunshine” (2006), won SAG ensemble and PGA honors and earned a DGA feature nom. The Oscars’ directing branch still shut them out.

	The Safdie brothers were similarly snubbed for “Uncut Gems” (2019), but when Josh Safdie made his solo debut with “Marty Supreme” last year, the branch gave him a nod. Even the Wachowskis couldn’t crack the category for the revolutionary technical achievement of “The Matrix” (1999).

	This season’s teams fit familiar types. Lord and Miller and Fielder and Oppenheim resemble the Daniels’ professional partnership, while the Esiri siblings are following the Coens’ path. Los Javis are the wild card: The couple’s roughly 13-year romantic relationship ended while they were making “La Bola Negra,” their most personal and ambitious collaboration.

	“The first question other directors will ask is ‘Why did you need two people to do this?’” one veteran strategist says. “The job is to convince a bunch of directors who often think they are the most creative artists alive that their genius can be shared. That’s tough.”

	None of the four teams is a conventional frontrunner. Fielder and Oppenheim are competing in a documentary lane the Directors Branch has always kept separate. Los Javis are more likely to make noise in international feature and screenplay because theirs is a non-English-language film. Lord and Miller are the closest thing to a studio-scale contender, but genre films need to overperform in below-the-line races to enter the conversation.

	Still, the sheer number of teams is the story. Four duos in one year reflects an industry increasingly built on shared creative enterprise, even as many directors cling to the myth of the solo genius.

	This week’s updated predictions are below.

body:
Nov 19, 2026 4:30pm PT	
	

	
	Oscar Predictions: Amanda Seyfried and Matt Damon Take the Top Spots for the First Time as Hollywood Heads Into Thanksgiving
	



			
			
	
						

									Hulu / Universal Pictures
	
					


							
		

	Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change based on buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.



	

					PRIMETIME, Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, 2026. © A24 / Courtesy Everett Collection
									Courtesy Everett Collection
	




	2027 Academy Awards Predictions Commentary All Categories (Updated: Nov. 19, 2026): Members of the Oscars are going into the Thanksgiving holiday with some homework to do, but they seem to have a clear road map for where to start.

	One of the final major variables of the fall, Netflix’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” premiered at the TCL Chinese Theatre on Nov. 16. Early reactions have been largely enthusiastic. That leaves the David Fincher-directed, Quentin Tarantino-penned film in roughly the same position it occupied heading into the premiere, but maybe it can pick up some heat.

	The awards calendar picks up quickly this week. 

	On Monday, the Critics Choice artisan shortlists will be released, offering the first meaningful read on the below-the-line races. That’s where “The Odyssey” and “Dune: Part Three” go head-to-head in production design, cinematography, sound and visual effects, while a scrappier contender could make its case before the guilds weigh in. 

	Then comes the season’s first major awards night: the Gotham Awards on Nov. 30. “The Invite” is among five films tied for the most nominations, with four apiece and shares the best feature lineup with “The Debut.” Both A24 Films appear on the Variety best picture list. 

	And then there’s the buzz still swirling around Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s “You Can See Everything.” For the first time this year, Amanda Seyfried takes the top spot in supporting actress and could be headed to a historic triumph if the buzz continues to grow. Also sitting in the No. 1 spot for the first time this year is Matt Damon’s work as Odysseus in Nolan’s “The Odyssey.” 

	Oh yeah, and Robert Pattinson is James Bond. 

	The announcement lands in the middle of the most acclaimed stretch of Pattinson’s career, with four films in contention for attention. But why does a casting announcement matter to an Oscar race? Because Oscars can be won on a single narrative. 

	Brendan Fraser (“The Whale”) had the comeback, same as Ke Huy Quan (“Everything Everywhere All at Once”). Quan’s co-star Jamie Lee Curtis had the body of work and a town that wanted to reward her. Voters like to feel they’re part of a “moment.” 

	What if this is Pattinson’s?

	It’s still early, and there’s still aways to go.

	This week’s updates are below.

	The 17th Governors Awards, honoring Close, Scott, Norman, Vachon and Koffler, take place Sunday, Nov. 15. Preliminary voting for the Oscar shortlists in 12 categories runs Dec. 7-11, with the shortlists announced Tuesday, Dec. 15. Following the close of the eligibility period on Dec. 31, nomination voting runs Jan. 11-15, 2027. The Academy will announce the official Oscar nominations Thursday, Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Oscars take place Sunday, March 14, 2027, with Conan O’Brien hosting for the third consecutive year. The ceremony airs live at 7 p.m. ET on ABC and in more than 200 territories worldwide from the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood.

title: Thomas Markle Confuses Meghan and Her Sister During Court-Ordered Psych Evaluation
description:
Thomas Markle
                          Confuses Meghan and Her Sister During Psych Eval
body:
Thomas Markle
                          Confuses Meghan and Her Sister During Psych Eval
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 19, 2026
                            4:44 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Thomas Markle didn't quite have his info straight during his court-ordered psych evaluation ... because he confused Meghan Markle and his other daughter.
      
    
              According to the forensic psychiatric evaluation obtained by TMZ ... Markle told the psychiatrist that he only has one daughter, when he actually has two.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              During the interview, Markle mentioned he had a son, Thomas Jr., and a daughter, Meghan.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The psychiatrist brought up Meghan's sister, Samantha, because he'd been staying with her, but Markle said ... "I don’t think so. I have two kids. I think Meghan is Samantha. I only have one daughter and one son."
      
    
              At another point, when talking about his psychiatric history, he referred to Meghan as his "sister," before apologizing and clarifying that he doesn't have a sister and that Meghan is his daughter.
      
    
              According to Page Six, Samantha went to a Tampa court Thursday to support her father in court, where a judge determined he's fit to stand trial.

                          Man Made Threats At Same Campus Where Charlie Kirk Was Killed
                          ... Suspect in Custody
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 19, 2026
                            5:21 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              A suspect is in custody after a man allegedly made threatening comments at Utah Valley University ... the same school where Charlie Kirk was shot and killed.
      
    
              The University issued an alert a little before noon about comments that were made in the Keller Building, where the business school is.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The man reportedly made the comments around 11:45 AM and left campus shortly after. The school said in the alert there was no active threat on campus.
      

              No word so far on what the so-called threatening comments actually were ... but UVU sent out another alert that afternoon saying the suspect had been arrested.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              The suspect hasn't been identified, but police previously described him as 6 feet tall with blonde hair and wearing a beanie.
      
    
              As you know ... Charlie Kirk was shot and killed while speaking at UVU on September 10, 2025.
